sentences.text: The shift to a cooked-food diet was a decisive point in human history.
The main topic of debate is when, exactly, this change occurred.

kotos.en: The shift to a cooked-food diet was a decisive point in human history.
kotos.t: 調理食への移行は人類史における決定的な転換点だった

kotos.en: The main topic of debate is when, exactly, this change occurred.
kotos.t: 主な論点は、その変化が正確にいつ起きたのかである（＝本文の問い）

sentences.text: All known human societies eat cooked foods, and biologists generally agree cooking could have had major effects on how the human body evolved.
( a1 ), cooked foods tend to be softer than raw ones, so humans can eat them with smaller teeth and weaker jaws.
Cooking also increases the energy they can get from the food they eat.
*Starchy potatoes and other *tubers, eaten by people across the world, are barely digestible when raw.
( a2 ), when humans try to eat more like chimpanzees and other primates, we cannot extract enough calories to live healthily.

Up to 50 percent of women who exclusively eat raw foods develop *amenorrhea, or lack of *menstruation, a sign the body does not have enough energy to support a pregnancy — a big problem from an evolutionary perspective.

kotos.en: All known human societies eat cooked foods, and biologists generally agree cooking could have had major effects on how the human body evolved.
kotos.t: 既知の人類社会はすべて調理食を食べており、生物学者は調理が人体の進化に大きな影響を与えたと概ね一致している

sentences.text: Such evidence suggests modern humans are biologically dependent on cooking.
But at what point in our evolutionary history was this strange new practice adopted?
Some researchers think cooking is a relatively recent innovation — at most 500,000 years old.
Cooking requires control of fire, and there is not much archaeological evidence for *hearths and purposefully built fires before this time.

kotos.t: こうした証拠は、現代人が生物学的に調理に依存していることを示す（¶2 のまとめ）

sentences.text: (b)The archaeological record becomes increasingly fragile farther back in time, however, so others think fire may have been controlled much earlier.
Anthropologist Richard Wrangham has proposed cooking arose before 1.8 million years ago, an invention of our evolutionary ancestors.
If the custom emerged this early, it could explain a defining feature of our species: the increase in brain size that occurred around this time.

sentences.text: What is the connection between cooking and brains?
Understanding how and why our brains got so big has been a major puzzle because such a brain is *metabolically expensive.
In fact, the brain needs more energy for its size than any other organ.
Although it might seem being smarter is always better, having a big brain exerts a high toll.
Ancestral humans may have compensated for this energy cost by cooking food.

kotos.en: What is the connection between cooking and brains?
kotos.t: 調理と脳のつながりは何か（¶4末の主張を掘り下げる問い）

kotos.en: Understanding how and why our brains got so big has been a major puzzle because such a brain is *metabolically expensive.
kotos.t: 脳がどう・なぜ大きくなったかは大きな謎だった。大きな脳は代謝的にコストが高いからだ

kotos.en: In fact, the brain needs more energy for its size than any other organ.
kotos.t: 実際、脳は大きさの割に他のどの器官より多くのエネルギーを必要とする

kotos.t: 賢い方が常に良いように思えるが、大きな脳は大きな代償を強いる

kotos.t: 祖先はこのエネルギーコストを、食物を調理することで埋め合わせたのかもしれない（調理仮説の核）

sentences.text: Like all ideas about human evolution, the cooking hypothesis can only be tested indirectly — without a time machine we cannot know exactly what happened in our evolutionary history.
But there are (c)several *converging pieces of evidence that support the cooking hypothesis.

kotos.en: Like all ideas about human evolution, the cooking hypothesis can only be tested indirectly — without a time machine we cannot know exactly what happened in our evolutionary history.
kotos.t: 人類進化のあらゆる説と同様、調理仮説は間接的にしか検証できない（タイムマシンがない以上、正確には分からない）

kotos.en: But there are (c)several *converging pieces of evidence that support the cooking hypothesis.
kotos.t: だが調理仮説を支持する、複数の収束する証拠がある（以下 ¶7 の列挙を予告）

sentences.text: Fossils show the teeth and *digestive tract of *Homo erectus decreased in size around the same time brain size increased.
This evidence likely means our ancestors started eating softer, higher-quality foods (although not necessarily cooked).
New archaeological research has also continued to push back the earliest known date for the control of fire.
For example, traces of purposeful fire at Wonderwerk Cave in South Africa have been dated at approximately a million years old.
Recent studies further suggest humans have genetic adaptions for eating cooked foods — some of which are old, at least predating our split from Neandertals.

Finally, some of my own work, with psychologist Felix Warneken, has shown chimpanzees possess many of the foundational cognitive capacities needed to start cooking — such as a preference for cooked food, patience to wait for foods to be cooked and the capacity to plan for and transport foods to a cooking site.
These data mean ancestral humans likely shared (d)the same abilities, and could have started cooking rapidly after gaining the ability to control fire.

kotos.en: Fossils show the teeth and *digestive tract of *Homo erectus decreased in size around the same time brain size increased.
kotos.t: 【証拠1・化石】ホモ・エレクトスの歯と消化管は、脳が大きくなったのとほぼ同時期に縮小した

kotos.en: This evidence likely means our ancestors started eating softer, higher-quality foods (although not necessarily cooked).
kotos.t: この証拠は祖先がより柔らかく質の高い食物を食べ始めたことを意味する（必ずしも調理とは限らない＝留保）

kotos.en: New archaeological research has also continued to push back the earliest known date for the control of fire.
kotos.t: 【証拠2・考古学】新しい研究は、火の制御が確認できる最古の年代を押し戻し続けている

kotos.t: 例えば南アフリカのワンダーワーク洞窟の意図的な火の痕跡は約100万年前と年代づけられている

kotos.t: 【証拠4・チンパンジー】筆者らの研究は、チンパンジーが調理を始めるのに必要な基礎的認知能力（調理食の選好・待つ忍耐・計画と運搬）の多くを持つと示した

sentences.text: These converging pieces of evidence point to an earlier date for the adoption of a cooked diet, in line with Wrangham's proposed time line.
But many exciting questions remain open.
How much of these changes were due to eating cooked foods specifically, versus the increased use of other processing techniques such as *pounding or cutting foods?
Did the adoption of cooking — generally a communal process in humans — require changes in our social behavior, given that other apes rarely share food?
Are there other ways to grow a big brain?
Answering these questions will continue to shed new light on human health, human psychology and the origins of our species.

kotos.en: These converging pieces of evidence point to an earlier date for the adoption of a cooked diet, in line with Wrangham's proposed time line.
kotos.t: これら収束する証拠は、調理食の採用がより早い時期だったことを示し、ラングハムの年代と一致する（＝説②を支持）
